template.title: Strongly regular graph srg({v}, {k}, {l}, {m})
template.statement: Find a graph on {v} vertices, {k}-regular, in which every two adjacent vertices have exactly {l} common neighbours and every two non-adjacent vertices exactly {m}: a strongly regular graph srg({v}, {k}, {l}, {m}). Its complement would be an srg({v}, {kc}, {lc}, {mc}), so either graph settles the question; submit the one with the parameters above.
template.submission: Text file: the graph in graph6 or sparse6 (as on House of Graphs), as an edge list (one edge "u v" per line, vertices numbered from 0) or as a 0/1 adjacency matrix.

score: 1 for a valid graph; none is known, so the best known value is 0
best_text: Brouwer's table marks these parameters '?': no graph is known and none has been ruled out, so the best known value is {best}; a valid graph scores 1.
holder_sources: the table's comments and references (srgtabrefs.html) give what is known about each case
open_rule: every parameter set the table marks '?' (existence unknown), counted once with its complement
left_out: 689 parameter sets marked '!' or '+' (a graph exists) and 384 marked '-' (ruled out), each with its complement
